card.name: Schuhplattler
card.era: Possible medieval roots; modern regulated form 19th c.
card.profile: The Schuhplattler is a folk dance of the Eastern Alps (Upper Bavaria, Tyrol, Salzburg) in which men stomp, clap and strike the soles of their shoes (Schuhe), thighs and knees with flat (platt) hands. It is often a couple dance: men perform leaps and slapping sequences to the Landler portion of the music in 3/4 time (originally zither and guitar, later accordion), while women in dirndls twirl; a boys-only form (reiner Burschenplattler) also exists. The tradition is preserved by Trachtenvereine (costume clubs) in Bavaria, Austria and German-immigrant communities worldwide (English Wikipedia; Society of Folk Dance Historians).
card.insight: Often said to mimic the courtship display of the Auerhahn (wood grouse); the modern form was popularized after locals performed it for King Maximilian II of Bavaria on 15 July 1858, and the first Schuhplattler society formed at Miesbach in 1861 (English Wikipedia).
